# 48433 Software Architecture — Assignment 2  
## Architecture and Quality Plan for the Campus Library Reservation System

## 1. Context and scope

The Campus Library Reservation System (CLRS) replaces the university’s ageing study-room reservation tool. It supports students and staff across three campus libraries. Students can search for rooms and equipment, create or modify reservations, cancel reservations, and receive reminders. Library staff can manage rooms, opening hours, block bookings and utilisation reports. Kiosks outside rooms display the current and next reservation.

The system must integrate with three existing systems:

- the university identity provider through SAML;
- facilities calendars through iCal feeds; and
- a read-only PostgreSQL room-inventory database.

The design must support the functional requirements FR-1 to FR-6 and the quality requirements QR-1 to QR-6. The most important architectural concerns are reliable reservation consistency, integration isolation, kiosk freshness, testability of reservation rules, performance during semester-start peaks, and simple deployment by a two-person team.
